t.4.64.1: Then, having heard Aṅgada's words, all those foremost of monkeys declared there, each in turn, his own ardent capacity for the journey.
t.4.64.2: Gaja, Gavākṣa, Gavaya, Śarabha and Gandhamādana, Mainda and Dvivida too, as well as Suṣeṇa and Jāmbavān.
t.4.64.3: Then Gaja spoke there: "I could leap ten yojanas." Gavākṣa said, "I shall go twenty yojanas."
t.4.64.4: Then the monkey Gavaya spoke to those monkeys: "O leapers, I shall go thirty yojanas."
t.4.64.5: Then the monkey Śarabha said to those monkeys: "I shall go forty yojanas; of this there is no doubt."
t.4.64.6: Then the greatly splendid Gandhamādana said to the monkeys: "I shall go fifty yojanas; of this there is no doubt."
t.4.64.7: Then the monkey Mainda said to those monkeys there: "I am able to leap a full sixty yojanas."
t.4.64.8: Then the greatly splendid Dvivida replied there: "I shall go seventy yojanas; there is no doubt."
t.4.64.9: But Suṣeṇa, the best of the monkeys, said to those most excellent of monkeys: "O bulls among the leaping ones, I could leap eighty yojanas."
t.4.64.10: While they were speaking there, Jāmbavān, the eldest among them, honoured them all and then replied.
t.4.64.11: Once we too had some prowess in movement; but now we have reached the far end of our years.
t.4.64.13: Now hear what my capacity for movement is, altered as it is by the change of time: I shall go ninety yojanas, of that there is no doubt.
t.4.64.12: But even when things have come to this, it is not possible to neglect this task, for the sake of which both the king of the monkeys and Rāma have made their firm resolve.
t.4.64.14: And Jāmbavān again spoke to all those foremost of monkeys: "Truly, my prowess in going was not always merely this much."
t.4.64.15: Long ago, at the sacrifice, the eternal Viṣṇu, Trivikrama, was circumambulated by me and by the mighty ones as he was taking his strides.
t.4.64.16: That same I am now old, feeble in my power of leaping; yet in my youth my strength was then unmatched by others.
t.4.64.17: At present I reckon my strength for going to be only this much, and with this much the accomplishment of this task will not come about.
t.4.64.18: Then the most wise Aṅgada, having shown respect to Jāmbavant, the great monkey, spoke a reply of noble meaning.
t.4.64.19: I shall go across this great distance of a hundred yojanas, but whether I would have the strength for returning or not is not certain.
t.4.64.20: To him Jāmbavān, the best of the monkeys and skilled in speech, said: "Your power in going is well known, O best of the monkeys and bears."
t.4.64.21: Granted, you are capable of going even a hundred thousand yojanas and returning again, but this is not declared to be the proper course.
t.4.64.22: For a master, the one who sends others, is by no means himself to be sent, dear one; all these people here are to be sent by you, O best of monkeys.
t.4.64.23: Established in the position of our master, you are our support. The master is the support of the army; this is the way of things, O scorcher of foes.
t.4.64.25: The root of one's purpose must be carefully guarded; this is the policy of those who know how to accomplish their tasks. For only when the root is intact do the benefits such as flowers and fruits come to fruition.
t.4.64.24: Therefore, dear one, you must always be protected as one protects a wife; moreover, you are the very root of this undertaking, O subduer of enemies.
t.4.64.27: You are indeed our preceptor and the son of our preceptor, O best of monkeys. Relying on you, we are surely capable of accomplishing our purpose.
t.4.64.26: Therefore you, whose valour is true, who are endowed with intelligence and prowess, O scorcher of foes, are the one through whom this task is to be accomplished here.
t.4.64.28: Then the great monkey Aṅgada, son of Vālin, gave a reply to the greatly wise Jāmbavant, who had spoken his words.
t.4.64.29: If I do not go, and no other bull among the monkeys goes, then this fast unto death must surely be undertaken by us once again.
t.4.64.30: For if we have not carried out the command of that wise lord of the monkeys, then even if we go back there, I see no way to protect our lives.
t.4.64.31: For that monkey is the master, utterly, both in his favour and in his wrath; if we go having transgressed his command, destruction would follow.
t.4.64.33: Then the heroic Jāmbavān, bull among monkeys, having been answered thus by Aṅgada, spoke these words in reply to Aṅgada.
t.4.64.32: Therefore, so that the course of this undertaking may not turn out otherwise, you yourself, who have grasped the matter, ought to think it through.
t.4.64.34: O hero, nothing of this task of yours shall fall short. Here I am urging on the one who will accomplish the task.
t.4.64.35: Then the foremost hero among the monkeys urged on Hanumān himself, that foremost hero of the monkeys, the renowned best of leapers, who had withdrawn to a secluded spot and was sitting at ease.
